findings.title: The named opening as a protective frame
findings.claim: The opening designation can be read as a frame for the story: the named God whose mercy the formula states is encountered later as protector and forgiver, and the family returns under that relation. A qualified source-variant coloring of name as raised mention meets the later scene in which Joseph raises his parents to honor.
findings.mechanism: The focus word for name/designation stands at the narrative threshold beside two divine mercy epithets. The context supplies a threatened separation at 12:9, calls Allah the best guardian at 12:64, joins pardon with mercy at 12:92, restores the parents and siblings at 12:99–100, and closes by calling the story guidance and mercy at 12:111. Separately, the lexicon's source-variant facet says that a name raises the named into notice; the parents' being raised to the throne at 12:100 supplies an analogical contact for that facet.
findings.reader_payoff: The name at the opening becomes more than a label: it helps the reader see the later protection and reunion under the mercy named at the threshold, with a bounded echo of the family's restored honor.
findings.containment: The focus word remains name/designation, and the formula remains an invocation in Allah's name. The raising facet is only the packet's etymological source-variant and its contact with 12:100 is analogical; it does not make the word lexically mean social elevation or claim that every event has one cause.

epistemic.reason: The trusted publication supports the protective narrative frame. The raised-designation detail comes through a legacy-unbound reading and is retained only as a qualified analogy under the lexicon's stated boundary.

findings.title: The named God as the point grief turns toward
findings.claim: The Allah named in the opening becomes the one to whom Jacob takes his grief and toward whom a late public call is directed, so the prefatory name is heard as a point of resort within the story.
findings.mechanism: The focus uses Allah as a proper name in the genitive phrase after bi-smi. At 12:86 Jacob says that he takes his distress and grief only to Allah; at 12:108 the call is directed toward Allah. Those independent uses make the proper name in the opening meet later acts of turning to God.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see where the story's grief is carried and where its later call points: to the same named God at the opening.
findings.containment: The focus occurrence remains a proper name in the prefatory construction, not a vocative form. Its role as refuge and direction is supplied by the later context and does not replace the plain sense.

epistemic.reason: The contact is directly visible in the supplied focus and context surfaces. The corresponding proper-name branch is marked qualified in the packet, and no direct vocative morphology is attributed to the focus occurrence.

findings.title: Mercy as the holding and repair of kinship
findings.claim: The paired divine mercy epithets can be read against the story's broken family ties as active care that preserves a bond through danger and lets the family re-form; the root's womb image adds a qualified picture of protective holding.
findings.mechanism: The focus epithets carry divine mercy. The family relations are placed under strain in Yusuf's address to his father and the warning about his brothers (12:4–5), then in the brothers' jealousy and plan (12:8–9). The later fear for Benjamin and appeal to divine protection (12:64), the removal of reproach (12:92), the parents' safe arrival, and the family's reunion (12:99–100) give the opening quality concrete people and acts. The distinct kinship branch meets those relations directly; the womb branch meets them only by analogy through its packet-defined image of carrying and holding a child. The closing description of the story as mercy (12:111) extends this reading to the narrative's stated benefit.
findings.reader_payoff: The opening's mercy becomes visible as care for a family carried from threatened bonds toward reunion, while the womb image remains a separate, bounded way to feel that holding relation.
findings.containment: The divine epithets retain their plain sense of mercy. They do not literally mean kinship or a womb; kinship is a contextual resonance, and the womb branch is an attributed analogy rather than a claim of pregnancy or anatomy in the story.

epistemic.reason: A trusted publication supports mercy as preserving and restoring kinship, and the packet directly supplies the family, protection, pardon, and reunion scenes. The womb-like holding relation is an explicitly bounded inference from legacy-unbound support.
